
**A spec heading is structure the spec owns.** It carries heading text and a depth at a position, and no body; its number and anchor are derived (WL-REQ-165). It groups the entries after it that sit deeper than it, and nothing else about it is stored. It is a `doc_rules` row with `heading` set and no `rule_id`, versioned with the spec's arrangement (WL-SPEC-77#sec-3a). It is not a rule: it has no ref, no versions of its own, no status and no edges, and plans cannot cover it or tasks be governed by it. A reference to its anchor (`WL-SPEC-77#sec-19`) resolves to the rules grouped under it (WL-SPEC-77#sec-4p). Renaming or moving a spec heading is an arrangement change and passes none of the in-place amendment gates (WL-SPEC-77#sec-10a, WL-SPEC-77#sec-10b).

On a spec write, an anchored heading followed directly by a deeper anchored heading, with no text in between, becomes a spec heading. An anchored heading with text becomes a rule, and the rule's text runs to the next anchored heading at any depth. A spec write is refused when it carries a heading within the anchor depth that has no anchor. Text before the first anchored heading, and text under a spec heading before its first deeper entry, is template text. Whether a passage is template text or a rule is the first test of WL-REQ-1367, applied by the author and checked at review; the store does not judge it. Headings deeper than the anchor depth stay content of the rule above them.
